answer: The passage says sparsity matters because real-world networks are often very sparse, meaning each node has only a small fraction of all possible connections. This makes it hard for standard machine learning methods to learn useful patterns directly from the raw graph structure, since there is little observed connectivity to work with. DeepWalk addresses this by learning low-dimensional vector representations of nodes from random walks over the network. These embeddings capture network structure and neighborhood relationships in a dense form, making the data easier to use for downstream machine learning tasks such as classification and clustering.
